acceptanceCriteria.statement: "on the galaxy screen there are many sectors in the grid that are not accessible, so there's wasted space" — at GALAXY, every part of the pane that looks clickable is clickable, and the galaxy that exists is on the glass. Design 1 wastes it one way (an 8x8 grid over a 216-texel square whose corners reach R~31 kpc, where no sector exists — the furthest of the 775 sits at R=21.2 kpc) and design 2 wastes it the opposite way (projection kind 'wide' crops the disc to a +/-11.33 kpc band, so about half of it is off-glass). BLOCKED ON MAX: which answer, decided on a rendered A/B, not on prose.

verifyVia.input: At GALAXY in each design, click at a sample of points across the whole map pane, including its extreme corners and its vertical edges.
verifyVia.observable: Every click inside the drawn map region resolves to a real sector, or lands on ground that is drawn as visibly outside the galaxy. No click inside a drawn grid cell returns null. In design 2 the disc's full vertical extent is reachable.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: "anything on screen should be clickable" — nothing is drawn in either design that does not answer a click. Today the rail's detail block, the status line, the y-gauge, design 2's minimap, the density bars, the HZ band, the orbit ellipses, the tile-ID plates, the prism's index tags and the placed labels are all inert.

verifyVia.input: In both designs, at every level, click each drawn element that is not already pickable.
verifyVia.observable: Each one either performs its own action (selects the object it names, scrolls to it, or drills) or is a readout deliberately and visibly marked as non-interactive. A published-geometry entry on S exists for every newly pickable element — the geometry comes out of the paint, never restated in the hit-test.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: "selecting one thing should not prevent a second selection, as is currently the case on the system screen" — at SYSTEM, clicking a body and then a different body moves the selection to the second one, in both designs. MEASURED ROOT CAUSE: selecting a planet that has moons sets _systemMode='planet', and NavComputer.js:4512-4522's 'planet' branch then writes { planetIndex: this._selectedPlanetIdx } — the already-selected planet — instead of this._hoveredBody.index. The legacy planet-detail view draws only the selected planet so the two agreed; the designs keep drawing all 15 bodies and keep publishing them all as pickable, so the selection sticks forever.

verifyVia.input: At SYSTEM in each design, click body A, then body B, then body C — including at least one body that has moons, since that is what arms the bug.
verifyVia.observable: nav._selectedBody follows each click. Measured today in design 2: three clicks on Sol b, Sol g and Sol b left _selectedBody frozen at planetIndex 3 every time.

acceptanceCriteria.progress: ✅ VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-07, design 1 at SYSTEM on Sol. Five clicks on five different planets — indices 1, 3, 1, 5, 0 — and _selectedBody followed EVERY one (1,3,1,5,0), with _systemMode staying 'system' throughout. Before the fix the same walk froze at planetIndex 3 in both designs.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: "it's important to be able to rotate it in 3D. The previous system for the prism view was more functional in that sense" — dragging on the PRISM screen turns the star column in 3D, in both designs, WITHOUT losing the low-fi look Max asked for by name. The rotation applies to the existing texel-quantised marks; it is not a switch back to the legacy renderer's arcs and strokes. MEASURED: _handleMouseMove already writes _localRotX/_localRotY on drag and the designs are blind to them — with a live control (moving _localCenter.z moved every published prism mark), changing _localRotX/_localRotY moved none.

verifyVia.input: At PRISM in each design, press and drag across the map pane.
verifyVia.observable: The star column turns with the drag: the published S.prismHits coordinates move as _localRotX/_localRotY change, and the marks stay texel-quantised (no anti-aliased arcs or sub-texel strokes appear).

acceptanceCriteria.progress: ✅ VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-07 with the same instrument and the same control as the pre-change measurement. The prism enters at _localRotX = 0.6521714117570698 (the derived default — the seed lands) and _localRotY = 0. Control still live (moving _localCenter.z moves every published mark). Rotating now MOVES the picture where before it was byte-identical, and returning the rotation restores the marks exactly.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: "clicking on a cell from the grid should highlight it, then zoom into it, resulting in the next screen (galaxy > sector > region)" — the clicked cell lights up FIRST, then the map flies into it. MEASURED: the zoom half is already live — a real GALAXY drill walks S.view.size 44 -> 43.98 -> 43.88 -> 43.63 -> 43.16 -> 42.46 -> 40.23 -> ... -> 0.5 and lands at SECTOR. What does not exist is any click-highlight state at all.

verifyVia.observable: The clicked cell is drawn highlighted before the view starts moving, and the highlight is visible for the first frames of the zoom.

acceptanceCriteria.progress: ◐ PARTLY VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-07. At SECTOR, a cell click set S.pick to '1:3,2' and it held across all 8 sampled frames, then cleared exactly when the drill landed (level 1 -> 2, viewSize 1 -> 0.125). ⛔ STILL MISSING AT GALAXY, which is the level Max named: at level 0 the cell is not the drill target (the identity is the containing sector, 1 of 775 and irregular, flying to its own centre and size), so framing the cell would promise the wrong destination. Needs the sector's own rect published out of the paint.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: "We have also lost much of the animation between screens" — the transitions that still SNAP animate too. MEASURED: _handleClick's tab-strip branch (NavComputer.js:4450) only calls _startDrillAnim when `idx <= 2 && this._levelIndex <= 2`; every transition touching PRISM (3) or SYSTEM (4) takes the else branch and jumps.

verifyVia.input: In each design, move between every adjacent pair of levels via the tab strip and via a drill click — REGION->PRISM and PRISM->SYSTEM especially.
verifyVia.observable: Each transition is animated rather than an instant cut.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: "I want to be able to grab and drag the system line view to look at the further planets from the star, rather than having to press a button exclusively" — at SYSTEM in design 1, dragging sideways scrolls the ladder. Today S.ladderScroll moves only on ',' / '.' and on a click in the two '...' cap zones. The drag must land on a published stop (S.ladderStops), never on a continuous offset, or it scrolls to a position with no body in it.

verifyVia.input: At SYSTEM in design 1, press on the ladder and drag left and right.
verifyVia.observable: The ladder scrolls with the drag and comes to rest on a body, not between bodies. The '1-14 OF 15' counter tracks it. The ',' / '.' keys and the cap clicks still work.

acceptanceCriteria.progress: ✅ VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-07, design 1 at SYSTEM. A leftward drag on the ladder took S.ladderScroll 0 -> 4 (its max on Sol) and left _systemRotX/_systemRotY untouched — so the gesture routes by design exactly as intended.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: "On the orbits view of the system screen, I want to be able to rotate the view in 3D like I could with the previous one" — at SYSTEM in design 2, dragging turns the orrery in 3D. _handleMouseMove already writes _systemRotX/_systemRotY on drag at level 4; d2System ignores them and uses a fixed TILT=0.42. ⛔ ONE GESTURE, TWO MEANINGS: the same drag pans design 1's ladder (AC-7) and rotates design 2's orrery. verifyVia.input: At SYSTEM in design 2, press and drag across the orbit view.
verifyVia.observable: The orrery's tilt and heading follow the drag; the published S.bodyHits coordinates move with _systemRotX/_systemRotY. Dragging in design 1 at the same level scrolls the ladder instead and does not rotate anything.

acceptanceCriteria.progress: ✅ VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-07, design 2 at SYSTEM. Entered at _systemRotX = asin(0.42) = 0.43344532006988595, _systemRotY = 0. A drag took them to 0.6254 / 0.5743, S.sysCam followed both, and the published body marks moved with them.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: "The indicators on the prism and system screens should be grabbable" — the readouts that show a position along a range are handles, not decoration. On the prism that is the y-gauge and the zoom/index indicators; at SYSTEM it is the ladder's scroll indicator and the counter.

verifyVia.input: At PRISM and at SYSTEM in each design, press on each indicator and drag along its axis.
verifyVia.observable: The indicator moves under the pointer and the view it reports moves with it. Releasing leaves the view where the indicator was dropped.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: FOUND IN PASSING, and it is a thing on the glass that is wrong: every body name in both designs is a silent error fallback, and past ten planets it reads 'Sol undefined'. state.js:109's makeRng returns { next, child } while NameGenerator's generatePlanetName / generateMoonName call rng.float() and rng.pick() — so every call throws, state.js:258-259's catch swallows it, and the fallback alphabet 'bcdefghijk' runs out at index 10. Sol has 13 planets. The comment at state.js:107 claims this rng is "the same shape" as NavComputer._makeRng (:315-327), which has float/int/pick/bool/chance; it is not.

verifyVia.input: At SYSTEM on Sol in design 1, read the ladder's body labels and the status line, scrolling to the outermost bodies.
verifyVia.observable: No body is named 'Sol undefined'. Names come from the real generator, not the catch-block fallback — verifiable headlessly by asserting makeRng exposes float/int/pick/bool/chance and that generatePlanetName does not throw.

acceptanceCriteria.progress: ✅ VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-07 on Sol. Zero names contain 'undefined'. The fifteen laddered bodies now read Veli, Sol Minor, Raupo, Sol e, BELT A, Sol f, Kothionura, Sol-7, Sol i, Sol j, Kezex, BELT B, Felfefeon, Flevonein, Zamioxkaho — the real generator's output. acceptanceCriteria.statement: THE REGRESSION GUARD, and it is the discipline that made the camera safe to wire last session: every rotation, drag and highlight added here leaves the DEFAULT picture exactly where Max ruled on it. Each view opens at the rotation it opens at today (_localRotX=0.5/_localRotY=0.3 at PRISM, _systemRotX=0.5/_systemRotY=0 at SYSTEM, against the designs' fixed rx=0.92/tilt=0.42), and only a real gesture changes it. ⚠ _localRotY is unclamped and unwrapped — it grows without bound across drags and must be wrapped now that the designs read it.

verifyVia.input: Enter each level in each design and render without touching the mouse or keyboard; then drag, then re-enter.
verifyVia.observable: The entry frame is byte-identical to the pre-change build's entry frame at every level in both designs. viewMode === null is today's nav, byte for byte. _localRotY stays bounded across many drags.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: FOUND IN PASSING, and it is live today without any rotation: design 2's orrery places every body at `a = i * 1.7 + 0.6` (d2System, lab:1406) where `i` is the DRAW-LOOP INDEX, not an orbital angle — and state.js:401 re-sorts D.bodies on [ / ] (AU / NAME / TEMP). So pressing the sort key at SYSTEM teleports every planet around its ring. The real angle exists and is simply dropped: StarSystemGenerator.js:550/609 and SolarSystemData.js:723/846 put `orbitAngle` on the planet wrapper and the LEGACY orrery already reads it (NavComputer.js:2853); buildBodies (state.js:265) never copies it across. ⚠ Fixing it MOVES EVERY PLANET in design 2's orrery — a change to a picture Max ruled on, so it goes to him as a rendered A/B.

verifyVia.input: At SYSTEM in design 2, note where each planet sits on its ring, then press [ and ] to cycle the sort key.
verifyVia.observable: Every body stays on its own ring at its own angle across every sort. The angles match the legacy orrery's, because both read the same p.orbitAngle.

acceptanceCriteria.progress: ✅ BUILT AND VERIFIED, ▶ AWAITING MAX'S RULING ON THE PICTURE. Bodies now read b.ang from the real p.orbitAngle. ⚠ It changes a picture Max ruled on, and the A/B is in shots/ with an honest read: A (old) looks better, B (real) is correct, and B clusters Sol's inner planets so their labels overlap where A's are clean.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: FOUND IN PASSING, and it is a live MIS-SELECTION, not an inert region: placeLabel (lab:296-306) walks 7 vertical offsets up to 18 texels from the star it labels and checks each candidate slot only against OTHER ALREADY-PLACED LABELS — never against star dots. So a label can land squarely on an unrelated star's mark, and clicking it selects the wrong star. The prism's index tags have the same drift at a fixed +3,-6 offset, over a field of up to 240 marks with a 3-texel hit radius.

verifyVia.input: At PRISM in design 2, find a placed star label that has drifted away from its own mark, and click the label.
verifyVia.observable: The star the label NAMES is selected — not whatever mark happens to lie under the label's plate. S.labelHits is tested before S.prismHits, so the plate's texels belong to the label's own object.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: FOUND BY THE NEW MARK GUARD, and nothing else could have seen it: design 2's moon pips are a SCREEN-SPACE strip drawn at `x + 4 + m*2, y - 4` (d2System:1416), so a moon-rich planet sitting on an outer orbit near cos(a) ~ 1 runs the strip off the right edge of the map. It was silently CLIPPED before, because rect/sprite/dottedEllipse were unguarded — assertFits is reached only through T() and therefore plated(). Zero firings at the default tilt, which is exactly why no suite is red today; 30 firings across a 1200-frame rotation sweep. The pips are correct as a screen-space badge and must stay one — the fix is to place the strip on whichever side of the body has room, not to tilt it into an ellipse.

verifyVia.input: Sweep the orrery through its full rotation range on a system with a moon-rich outer planet (the lab's own Q/E and arrow keys drive it).
verifyVia.observable: assertMark reports zero overflows at every angle, and the moon pips stay on the glass rather than being clipped at the pane edge.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Max walks both nav menus again, screen by screen, and each one holds up close.

verifyVia.input: ORRERY -> N -> V, then walk GALAXY / SECTOR / REGION / PRISM / SYSTEM in both designs, clicking and dragging everything.
verifyVia.observable: Max's judgment that the screens hold up. NEVER driven or PASSed by an agent.

inputs: nav-240p-lab.html — THE SPEC. Every design change goes here and is re-extracted; designs.js is GENERATED and must never be hand-edited.

src/ui/NavComputer.js — the host. LINE-COUNT-FROZEN at 4711; ~700 line-anchored citations ride it, so new statements FOLD onto existing lines and every comment on a folded line must be /* */ terminated. Lines 586, 4345, 4420 and 4442 end in // and are poisoned. The keyboard fold line is 349.

NavComputer's live drag state — _dragging, _dragStartX/Y, _dragStartRotX/Y, _localRotX/_localRotY (PRISM), _systemRotX/_systemRotY (SYSTEM). All already written at 0.008 rad/px on drag; the designs simply never read them.
src/ui/navViewModes/state.js — the adapter that builds S and D. S.cam and S.view are the pipes the camera and the 2D frame already travel down; rotation is one more field on S.cam.
src/ui/navViewModes/index.js — the driver: modes, buffer, the render-tail hover picker, the keyboard methods, remapClick.
src/ui/navViewModes/picking.js — hit-testing over what the paint published; branches on S.mapProj.kind in exactly one place.
src/generation/NameGenerator.js — generatePlanetName / generateMoonName, whose rng contract state.js does not currently satisfy (AC-10).
outputs: The two 240p nav view modes ('rail' and 'bars') as the player drives them — both ship, per Max's 'I like both versions... let's keep both'.
S.cam gains rotX/rotY; d2System gains a real camera; new published-geometry fields on S for every element AC-2 makes pickable and for the AC-5 click-highlight.

The diegetic cockpit nav panel eventually represents these designs — ⛔ but it MUST NOT change here. Two NavComputer instances exist (main.js:4700 and :5895); the gate is activate(), which _openCockpitNav never calls. NOT _bare, which is permanently false on the panel.
mustStayWorking: node scripts/extract-nav-designs.mjs --check exits 0 — designs.js matches the lab.
viewMode === null is today's nav, byte for byte.

Suites at baseline: tests/ 20 failed across the same 8 files (agent-camera-api, driver-pack-giantdeck, gas-body-lab-material, lab-shader-perframe-seam, moon-condition-contract, moon-rng-stream-identity, port-condition-contract, relief-octave-lod-ramp); src/cockpit 698 passed; src/ui 520 passed (baseline moved 480 -> 520 when the three build agents landed 40 new tests). ⚠ navViewModes.test.js's 'rail: every level tab changes level when clicked where it is drawn' failed once under a full src/ui run and passed 3/3 in isolation — cross-test pollution, pre-existing, not caused here.

AC-1..AC-11 of the closed nav-menu-elements-functional workstream: the map is a picker at all five levels in both designs; Tab / Enter / [ ] / - = / / stay bound; the prism follows the camera on WASD/R/F and the wheel; the drawn search reuses the whole existing search pipeline.

Hover resolves at the TAIL of the driver's render() — the legacy painters rewrite all three hover fields every frame from _mouseX/_mouseY against LEGACY geometry, so any new pointer state must be written there too or the legacy pass wins.
The legacy renderer keeps running underneath every mode frame ON PURPOSE — it is also the lazy loader (_renderLocal -> _ensureStarsLoaded; _renderSystem resolves _systemData).
_autopilotButtonRect is a live invisible button that _handleClick tests FIRST; any new interactive rect competes with that ordering.

A painter throw freezes the glass — PanelHost catches once, then stops uploading, and the screen keeps showing the last good frame and looks alive. Every new field the designs read needs a default in state.js.
S and D are MUTATED, never replaced — a fresh object leaves every design painting the frame the factory was built on, forever, and it repaints happily.
